title: Friendship with Bechet and recordings
summary: They became close friends; Goudie visited Bechet in Paris after the war and discusses recordings with Noble Sissle.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Well, I was there when it happened and he had to leave and I had to bring that up, but it's the truth anyway. The truth can be put on that. It's living. And when he came back, he, ten years after that, he came back and he, when he went, when he got out and I wanted to help him. He said, if you need anything, just let me know. And he never forget that he saw that. I really meant to be in his corner and be his friend. You know? And that's why he received me when he came back. Oh, yeah. Ten years after. I never known Sidney. Been very close to him. I made some recording with him, I think. No, but Sissy. What do you want with him? Some records with Sisley? Sisley.
Sisley. Yeah. No, not with Sidney. Oh, I thought Sidney was a good one. I was a good one. I was a good one.
Sidney. Oh, I thought Sidney was in that.
In one. No. That was Sidney that was in 29. Yeah. Or 30 or 31 somewhere.
Oh, you made some black stick in some of those. You were on Alba Sax, were you? Or...
Alba Sax. But Sidney was with Noble before then. I think Sidney, John Noble, Sissel, I think in 28, oh 27, 90, somewhere long there anyway.
